newsitem.title: TURKEY: U.S. envoy to meet Iraq Kurds in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to meet Iraq Kurds in Turkey.

text.p: U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau is to hold separate talks in Turkey this week with two Iraqi Kurdish leaders in a bid to end the inter-Kurdish conflict in north Iraq, Turkish officials said on Sunday.

Pelletreau was to arrive in Ankara later on Sunday on his way to southeast Turkey for a meeting on Monday with Iraqi Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani, who allied himself with Baghdad forces in August to drive a rival group from the main regional city of Arbil.
"Tomorrow morning he is going to the southeast to meet Barzani," a Turkish foreign ministry official in Ankara told Reuters.
He said Pelletreau, the assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs, would meet Barzani's rival Jalal Talabani, head of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), in Ankara on Tuesday.
The United States has urged an immediate ceasefire between the two groups in fighting that has damaged U.S. interests in north Iraq and threatened to bring in Iraq and Iran.
Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) has won back much of the ground it lost to Talabani's group in clashes last week and was moving on the PUK's stronghold of Sulaimaniya.
Hundreds of Kurds who worked for U.S.-affiliated organisations were evacuated to Turkey from Iraq at the weekend, Turkish border officials said.

Around 700 Kurds, including relatives, poured through the Habur border crossing overnight on their way to a temporary camp in the Turkish town of Silopi. Turkish customs officers and two U.S. officials questioned them on their arrival, witnesses said.
Washington last month evacuated more than 2,000 Kurds who had worked for U.S. military, aid and intelligence programmes in northern Iraq after Baghdad intervened in the Kurdish fighting.
Despite claims by both Iraqi Kurdish groups of Iranian and Iraqi involvement in this month's fighting, there has been no sign of such involvement.
